title: How to resolve missing supplier certificates before material is needed
summary: Identify the required certificate, match it to the correct shipment and lot, obtain missing evidence, and hand it to quality for disposition.
body_markdown:
Resolve a missing supplier certificate by identifying the exact document requirement, the affected material and lot, and the quality owner who will decide whether the evidence is acceptable. Ask the supplier for that specific document, link the response to the receipt, and follow the issue through the quality disposition. Receiving a PDF is a document event; it is not permission to release material.


Use the[supplier certificate follow-up and quality handoff form (Excel)](https://www.mandel.ai/resources/missing-supplier-certificates.xlsx) to keep the request precise. It is designed for procurement coordination, not for determining technical compliance or replacing your quality procedure.


## Establish what is actually required


Read the approved PO, specification, quality agreement, and applicable receiving instruction. Identify the requirement source and revision, required document type, material scope, issuer, timing, and any lot or shipment linkage. Have the quality owner resolve unclear requirements.


Different documents answer different questions. A requested certificate of analysis, certificate of conformity, material test report, or manufacturer record should not be treated as interchangeable simply because each is called a certificate. Ask quality to state the acceptable evidence for this material and purchase.


Do not create a new certificate requirement from a generic checklist after the order has shipped. If the requirement was omitted or ambiguous in the purchase package, record the gap and route the needed supplier request and commercial implications to the appropriate owners.


SAP documents certificate receipts against purchasing documents and delivery information, including recording certificates before the goods arrive. That provides useful system support for keeping documents and material connected.[SAP certificate receipt documentation](https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_ON-PREMISE/2bc3ee8d1c83404e8cf62418640004f2/646dbbf63afd44588da4df24dc608995.html?locale=en-US) .


## Identify the affected quantity and physical status


Record the PO line, item, specification revision, supplier, manufacturer where relevant, shipment, packing slip, lot or batch, quantity, unit, and destination. Confirm whether the goods are unshipped, in transit, at the dock, under inspection, or already otherwise dispositioned.


Determine whether one document is expected per lot, per shipment, per receipt, or under another rule defined by quality. If the same lot arrives twice, a valid document may be reusable under your process, but that decision needs to be explicit. If a shipment contains two lots, one certificate may cover only one.


Attach the missing-document work to the affected quantity. A 1,000-unit PO should not necessarily be treated as entirely blocked because a 200-unit lot lacks evidence. Equally, a certificate for 200 should not be used to imply that the remaining 800 is covered.


Ask planning for the usable-material need date and ask quality for its review lead time and current capacity. These establish the document decision deadline. Procurement should not assume immediate release once the file arrives.


## Search the expected channels before requesting a duplicate


Check the approved evidence locations: supplier portal, PO thread, shipment attachments, quality inbox, and existing certificate receipt record. Ask receiving whether a paper copy accompanied the delivery, then use the approved process to capture it.


Search by the material and lot identifiers as well as the PO. A manufacturer’s certificate may reference its own part and lot numbers rather than the buyer’s order. Preserve the mapping evidence; do not rename a file and treat that as proof of applicability.


If you find two versions, keep both and identify which supersedes the other. A corrected result or lot reference needs explanation from the issuer and quality review. Do not discard the earlier version just because the later PDF appears cleaner.


If the document is already in the system but the receipt link is missing, assign the linking correction to the authorized owner. Avoid chasing the supplier for a document the team already possesses while the real problem is internal routing.


## Ask the supplier for an identifiable document


Send a bounded request with enough information to locate the record. Reference the requirement and state what is missing without making a technical conclusion yourself.


```text
Subject: Certificate needed — PO [number], line [line], lot [lot]


For [item/specification revision], shipment [reference], [quantity/unit],
we need [document type] required by [approved requirement reference].
The material is currently [physical status] at [site].


Please provide the document covering lot [lot] by [date/time/time zone].
The file received on [date] covers [other lot / missing field] instead.
If the requested record is unavailable, state the reason and the
earliest date it can be provided. Please identify the issuing party.


```


Do not ask the supplier to edit a certificate to match your tracker. If an identifier is wrong, ask the issuer to investigate and provide the appropriate correction or explanation. Preserve the original document and the response.


Set an internal handoff deadline before the material need, allowing the review time quality has specified. If that is no longer achievable, open an operational recovery decision in parallel rather than promising that the document will solve the shortage in time.


## Check administrative completeness and hand off to quality


Procurement can check whether the response is readable, complete as a file, connected to the requested identifiers, and accompanied by an explanation for any apparent mismatch. Record missing pages, unclear lot references, or missing attachments as questions.


Quality owns the technical content review, authenticity assessment where required, acceptability, and release or other disposition. A procurement reviewer or automation may extract a test result; that does not confer authority to decide whether the material passes.


Microsoft documents inventory blocking during quality processes to prevent unapproved use. Follow the controls your organization has configured and assigned to the responsible functions.[Microsoft quality management overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/supply-chain/inventory/quality-management-processes) .


Give quality the requirement source, material and receipt identifiers, all relevant document versions, supplier explanation, affected quantity, and need date. Ask for a disposition or specific further evidence request by a defined time. “Document attached” without these links pushes the investigation to quality.


## Worked example: two lots, only one certificate


In this illustrative example, 600 kilograms of a specified material arrive under one PO line: 400 kilograms from lot A and 200 from lot B. The approved quality instruction requires a certificate of analysis for each lot. The supplier sends a document covering A only.


Receiving records both quantities and lots. Procurement opens one missing-document request for B’s 200 kilograms, linking the packing slip and quality requirement. Quality reviews A’s evidence and releases A through its normal process; B remains under its assigned quality status.


Planning needs 450 kilograms usable by Thursday noon. With only A’s 400 released, the immediate gap is 50, not the full 600 and not automatically B’s full 200. Quality says it needs four working hours to review B once a complete record arrives. The buyer therefore asks for B’s document early enough to preserve that review window.


The supplier replies Wednesday afternoon with a certificate for lot B-1. The packing slip and container labels say B-2. Procurement records the mismatch and asks the supplier to reconcile the identifiers. It does not change the tracker to B-1 to make the file match.


The supplier’s quality contact identifies an attachment error and sends the B-2 certificate Thursday at 9 a.m. The four-hour review allowance would extend past the noon need. Planning therefore considers an approved stock transfer for the 50-kilogram gap while quality reviews B-2. Collection of the correct file has improved the evidence position, but it has not yet solved the timed supply requirement.


At 11 a.m., quality completes its review and releases B’s 200 kilograms. The authorized inventory process records the disposition. Planning confirms all 450 required kilograms are now available before noon and cancels the unused transfer request through the proper process. The final trail retains the wrong attachment, correction, quality decision, and inventory reference.


If quality had rejected B-2 or requested more evidence, the document chase would remain tied to that decision and planning would continue recovery. There is no automatic release after a timer expires.


## Handle evidence that remains incomplete or disputed


**The supplier says it never promised the document.** Find the approved requirement and send the reference. If the order package does not establish it, route the gap to the buyer and quality owner. Do not invent a contractual obligation in the follow-up.


**The supplier can provide a generic certificate only.** Ask quality whether it meets the actual requirement and what additional linkage is needed. A generic company certificate may answer a supplier-qualification question without identifying the delivered lot.


**The supplier cannot obtain the manufacturer record.** Capture the reason, the earliest feasible route, and any proposed alternative evidence. Quality decides whether alternatives are acceptable. The buyer decides whether to pursue replacement supply or another commercial outcome.


**The document appears inconsistent or altered.** Preserve the received file, stop treating it as verified evidence, and route it to the appropriate quality or investigation owner. Obtain clarification through established contacts. Procurement should not “repair” values in the file.


**Material is urgently needed.** Present the shortage quantity, timing, evidence gap, review status, and alternatives. Any deviation or release decision belongs to the authorized process. Urgency does not transfer that authority to the person doing the chasing.


## Keep supplier waiting separate from internal review


Use distinct states: requirement unclear, document missing, supplier clarification pending, received for review, quality decision pending, correction requested, and disposition complete. A received document can move the work from the supplier to quality without closing the material issue.


Give each state a next action and owner. If quality asks a technical question, send that exact question to the appropriate supplier contact and link the reply back. Avoid repeated forwarding of the whole thread without saying what answer is needed.


For recurring missing documents, review the ordering and dispatch instructions. Add an approved pre-dispatch checkpoint or receiving linkage where useful. Correct the process that repeatedly leaves the same requirement out; do not merely increase reminder frequency.


## Measure evidence coverage and release outcomes separately


Define evidence coverage as required lot-or-receipt document sets received and administratively linked, divided by all required sets in the due cohort. Define quality disposition completeness separately as those sets with a recorded quality decision divided by the same cohort. State which unit you count and how split lots are handled.


For ten required lot sets, nine documents received and seven quality decisions means 90% document coverage and 70% disposition completeness. It does not mean 90% of material is acceptable. Show affected quantities and need dates alongside counts because lots can differ substantially in size and importance.


Track supplier wait, internal review wait, wrong-document returns, and unresolved age. Use the results to improve instructions and handoffs. Do not describe a faster file retrieval time as a reduced quality review requirement.


## Close with a linked disposition


Close the missing-document task when the required evidence has an accepted administrative and quality disposition, the correct material record is linked, and any follow-on supply or commercial work has an owner. If the final disposition is rejection or return, retain that outcome rather than labeling it a successful release.


Mandel’s[purchase order management](https://www.mandel.ai/use-cases/purchase-order-management) work can coordinate missing evidence and supplier follow-up. Quality retains material acceptance and release; the buyer gets a complete record and a clear next decision.
